Grounding Totem is a Restoration shaman PvP talent. It applies a buff to all party members within range which effectively makes one party member immune to the next spell cast on them, apart from AoE spells. This spell will affect the totem instead, destroying it.

__NOTOC__ Grumnus Steelshaper is a dwarf blacksmithing trainer. He is located at the center of the Great Forge in Ironforge. He was originally an armorsmith specialization trainer. By the time of the Fourth War, Grumnus had retired and moved to Thelsamar in Loch Modan. He was called on to reforge the Bulwark of the Mountain King, the armor of Madoran Bronzebeard.

The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred ruin of an old night elven temple, where Onu, an Ancient of Lore, resides together with a pair of merchants and a sleeping druid. The grove lies in the southeastern part of Darkshore, nestled near the mountains, and is built around the surging Wildbend River. The Circle of Ancients meets here.

Grub is an orc located in a hut just east of the Crossroads at the foot of a mountain in the Northern Barrens. He appears to own the building with Duhng as his cook and Tarban Hearthgrain as his baker. During the Legion Invasions, he was cowering in fear behind Guard Taruc.
Grundig Darkcloud is an elite tauren found in Grimtotem Post in the Stonetalon Mountains. He led an attack on Camp Aparaje.

__NOTOC__ Groth is the only orc in Harkyn Grymstone's bounty-hunter team. Although not skilled with guns (unlike his two troll companions and his boss) he is an excellent tracker and a powerful warrior. His two-handed axe saved the group countless of times whilst fighting the Scourge. He and Harkyn are shown to be partners and the group's planners. It is believed this orc is Harkyn's second in command.
Gryfe is the flight master located at Marshal's Stand in the territory of Un'Goro Crater.

Gruff Slategray is a dwarven buccaneer. Dwarves don't go to sea. Dwarves do not become pirates. And yet tales exist of Gruff Slategray. Kidnapped for his skill in making firearms, he supplies a pirate gang with guns. Once, when the Alliance attacked, Gruff realized that although he was a prisoner, he had to help keep the ship afloat in order to survive. So he climbed to the top of the mast with a rifle he got off a dead body and shot Alliance sailors who were attempting to set fire to the ship. It broke his heart a little bit each time he shot one down, and now he lives a life of self-loathing, missing his mountains, but forced to aid the pirates when they come under fire. __NOTOC__ Grumbald One-Eye is a powerful furbolg shaman found at Heart's Blood Shrine in Grizzly Hills.
__NOTOC__ Grunda Bronzewing is a dwarf flying mount vendor located at Honor Hold in Hellfire Peninsula. She sells gryphons.

The grummles are the humble wanderers of the mountains of Pandaria. They make good guides and can carry many times their own weight. They have a trade route that stretches across the zone called the Burlap Trail, which they will need adventurers' help with as this is a very dangerous area. The grummles regularly trade with the pandaren, bringing essential supplies to the Shado-Pan forces guarding the great Serpent's Spine wall, and for a happy-go-lucky people they take this task quite seriously. Such trade endeavors were established long ago, and have forged one of the strongest ties possible between two sapient species on Pandaria.

Thrall introduced himself as a warlock named Thra'kash who was sent to assist him with a secret mission. Grukar took him to a camp where Orgrim Doomhammer met with Durotan and Draka who told him about Gul'dan's betrayal. Grrbrrgle is found at inside A Restless Crate, washed up on a small island off the Sunset Shore off the southwest coast of Talador. A few Shipwrecked Smugglers landed with their cargo on a small boat, but none of them made it, and a warning note next to the crate explains why: Not that players are known for heeding warnings, interact with the crate anyway to release Grrbrrgle, a rare deep sea murloc. The murloc drops Mrglrgirdle and 10-20 Garrison Resources.

__NOTOC__ Grunt Arhung is an orc guard located at the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar. After the battle of the Broken Shore, he can be found alongside other concerned citizens of the Horde in front of Grommash Hold.
Gruesome Bite is a pet ability available exclusively to the riverbeast family of hunter pets, reducing the effects of healing on the target by 50%.

Grulloc's Lair is the lower levels of Grulloc's Grotto in Frostfire Ridge. It is where the gronn was placed after being captured by Hatock the Gronnmaster and the . When leads a group of Frostwolf Orcs to kill Hatock, the Thunderlord releases the gronn in order to destroy his enemies. In return with a leaping strike, Ga'nar blinds the massive gronn, leaving him to do little more than swing and stomp wildly in hopes of hitting something. An effort that proved futile as the gronn was slain, with Hatock following soon after.

Grumble, Worldshaker is an earth elemental found underground. He was born from the ambient magic soaking into the walls, and he wakes every few millennia, sending tremors and terror throughout the kobold empire.

The Groovy Abominations are two abominations located in the Auction House of the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar during the Forsaken round of the Auction House Dance Party.

Native to the Aerie Peak and the Hinterlands, they have long shared an inseparable bond with the dwarves of the Wildhammer clan, who later introduced them to the rest of the Alliance. Gryphon riders are mostly dwarves of the Wildhammer clan, but more recently Ironforge dwarves and humans alike have started deploying gryphon riders of their own. __NOTOC__ Guardians of Blizzard were World of Warcraft mobs that Blizzard Entertainment created to ward off curious players from entering unfinished zones during alpha and beta testing stage of the game. They usually appeared as infernals (but could be any number of different creatures, including rats); however, they are much more powerful. They possess a spell called Death's Touch which one-hits any player. This function also existed on mobs in any completely-closed, yet populated, zone during the earlier testing phases, since there were ways of easily getting past the Guardians.

As of patch 2.1, all potions and elixirs that added a buff were designated as either Guardian Elixirs or Battle Elixirs. The Guardian Elixirs being those that increase your defense, stamina, protection, mana regen, armor, etc. Elixirs will stack with ability-generated buffs (Arcane Intellect for example) but will not stack with other Guardian Elixirs. Players can only have one Guardian Elixir and one Battle Elixir active on them at one time, or one Flask, which counts as both Elixir slots. Review the Elixir article for a full list of items classified in-game as Guardian Elixirs.

Guardian eyes (aka floating eyes and occuli) are animate, demonic eyeballs that accompany the inquisitors. They are summoned by them from the Twisting Nether. They come in green, red and blue colors. The Guard of Suramar (or the Suramar Guard, Suramar's Watch, or simply the Watch) was the night elf organization of troops who fought and defended the city of Suramar. Jarod Shadowsong rose to the rank of a captain by the time of the War of the Ancients. Jarod was later placed under the command of Kur'talos Ravencrest. Suramar had only a small facility for prisoners, most of any import ending up in Black Rook Hold. The Guard's headquarters was created out of the base of a long dead tree. The roots formed the skeleton of the building and workers had created the rest from stone. There was no more solid a building than this save Lord Ravencrest's hold and the Suramar Guard were proud of that.

Guardsman Dorin is a deceased venthyr located at the Catacombs of Regret in Revendreth. He was tasked by Guard Captain Elizabeta to search for Watcher Emil, who hadn't been heard from since the catacombs erupted in chaos. Although Dorin was able to locate Emil, he was unable to get past the powerful sinstone constructs wandering the catacombs. Ultimately, he was attacked and presumably killed by scouts from Archivam. His journal can be found next to his body.

Guard Bahir is a centaur of Clan Nokhud initially found guarding the eastern entrance to the Nokhud encampment in Maruukai in the Ohn'ahran Plains. Scout Tomul (reluctantly) introduces adventurers to her so they can learn about the Nokhud, and Bahir sends the outsiders to "prove they're not as weak as they look" by participating in the tabarr. When the Nokhud reveal their alliance with the Primalists and betray the other clans, Balakar Khan leaves Bahir in charge to cover his escape from the city, and she moves to Maruukai's western entrance. Discovering ways to make money in World of Warcraft is an important part of getting the most enjoyment out of the game. There are many different and effective ways to make enough money for repairs, consumables, equipment, and other items. Some players attempt to purchase gold from third party gold sellers. This form of making money is against Blizzard Entertainment's terms of service and may lead to a permanent ban on an account. It may also lead to real world identity theft or theft of the purchaser's WoW account depending on the reliability and intentions of the gold selling company. There are four major money making strategies; farming, crafting, daily quests and using the auction house.

A guild master earns his or her living by charging money to assign potential guild leaders a charter with which they can form a guild. They are a special type of NPC that assists in starting guilds (purchasing Guild Charters), designing tabards and purchasing tabards. There is one guild master in each major city.

Gunther Weller is the co-owner of Weller's Arsenal with his (assumed) wife Marda Weller. He is a weapons vendor and can be found in their shop near the Stormwind auction house, just off the main square in the trade district of Stormwind City.

Gunther's Retreat is an island located in Brightwater Lake in central Tirisfal Glades. It is home to the Forsaken lich Gunther Arcanus and his zombie minions. On the southwestern side of the retreat is a small, unnamed islet holding Lillith's Dinner Table.
__NOTOC__ Gunther Arcanus is a powerful Forsaken lich located at Gunther's Retreat in the Tirisfal Glades.

A Guild Hall is a building historically used by guilds for meetings. In-game it is an instanced room for player housing. Currently this feature does not exist in World of Warcraft. The Explorers' Guild meets in a huge guildhall called the Explorers' Guildhall which is located in Ironforge. "Smaller guildhalls...are being established in far-flung corners of Azeroth, usually in the back rooms of inns or taverns along well-traveled routes to distant parts of the continent."

Gunny is a dwarf quest giver in both the Blood Furnace and the Shattered Halls, where he is wounded and cursed and ultimately succumbs to his wounds despite efforts to save his life. He originally appeared at Honor Hold in Hellfire Peninsula.
Gur'zil is a jungle troll flight master located at Swamprat Post in Zangarmarsh.

Gunstan's Dig is a small dwarven camp setup by the Explorer's League south of the Southmoon Ruins, just east of the Valley of the Watchers, in Tanaris. Unlike the Horde equivalent, Dawnrise Expedition, this Alliance camp is not an actual subzone.

Guild rewards are items purchased from guild vendors after gaining guild reputation and earning guild achievements. They should not be confused with guild perks, abilities automatically granted to guild members.
Guild Level 25 is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by reaching guild level 25.

Inviting a player to a guild requires a guild rank with permission from the Guild Master to recruit new members. If you have the ability to invite new members there are 2 basic ways to do it: * Use the Slash Command: /ginvite <player_name> * Use the Guild pane of the Friends List window: *# Click Add Member button (bottom-right of the window). *# Enter player name to invite to guild and click Invite.

Gutterspeak (known in-game as Forsaken) is the language of the Forsaken. Gutterspeak is a lower form of Common that uses little (very little) bits of Dwarven and Thalassian. It has existed for a while (longer than the undead Forsaken have), and evolved in the shady underground of black markets and rogues' guilds as the tongue spoken by people of ill-repute. When the Forsaken took the Undercity, they adopted Gutterspeak as their official language. One explanation would be that the Forsaken, discarded and abandoned by their loved ones, found it appropriate to adopt this language of the rejects of society. HP5 (also known as HP/5) is a shortened term for the item bonus "Restores X health per 5 sec." Although the number given is based on 5 second intervals, the effect will trigger every 2 seconds. For example, an item that grants 10 health per 5 sec will restore 4 health on every "tick". Health regeneration depends on Spirit and HP5 bonuses, in most cases Spirit only affects regen outside of the 5 second rule, while HP5 bonuses apply at all times.

Hakkar the Houndmaster is an agent of the Burning Legion and was the first major demon to cross the Well of Eternity portal. He supervised the portal's growth with Mannoroth during the War of the Ancients, and returned to create a powerful breed of mage-hunter felhounds during the third invasion of the Burning Legion.

Hakkar the Soulflayer, the Blood God, is a malevolent and destructive loa notably worshipped by the Gurubashi trolls, and known in the troll pantheon as the Loa of Blood. He at one point controlled the Gurubashi Empire's fallen capital of Zul'Gurub. Hakkar the Soulflayer was the final boss of the Zul'Gurub raid until it was removed with and Zul'Gurub was turned into an ordinary subzone of Northern Stranglethorn. Though the world believed Hakkar to be dead, there were rumors that the god might return one day. These ultimately proved true when the troll Jin'do brought back his spirit in order to drain the blood god's powers into himself. Hakkar's blood is very potent. A small amount of his blo

Half-orc is a term used to describe the half-breed offspring of an orc, or half-orc parent, and a parent of any other species. It most often refers to a half-orc half-human, but can also be used to refer to a half-orc half-ogre, or half-orc half-draenei. Half-breeds are rare in the Warcraft universe. Half-orc, half-draenei are reviled and scorned by both draenei and orc cultures. According to Lantresor of the Blade, his kind are a rare breed, with most having been killed decades ago. In the Old Horde, a clan of half-ogre half-orc named, the mok'nathal, were considered half-breeds and thus lesser than true orcs. However, times changed under the New Horde, and the inclusion of the mok'nathal a

Hakkari Witch Doctors are jungle trolls found in Zul'Gurub. Hakkari Witch Doctors have an ability to polymorph a target into a frog (Hex). Hexxed targets can still be attacked and will not break the Hex. If a Witch Doctor is part of a group with a Gurubashi Blood Drinker, the Witch Doctor can be mind controlled and Hex the Blood Drinker, neutralizing the AoE life drain and making the Blood Drinker easy to kill. They also summon toads.
The Hakkari Coin is a Paragon of Power sought after by the Zandalar Tribe.

Halaa is a small town on a plateau in Nagrand. It was the primary draenei research facility for the study of naaru crystals. The faction controlling the town receives a zone-wide +5% damage buff, and gains access to the NPCs spawned inside Halaa; the opposing faction can attempt to lay siege to Halaa by first killing all 15 of the NPC guards, then outnumbering the faction controlling Halaa on the island itself.
Halaani Bag is sold by Quartermaster Jaffrey Noreliqe or Quartermaster Davian Vaclav in Halaa for when their respective faction is in control of the city.

Half-night elves, or half-kaldorei, are the offspring of night elves and another species (such as humans). Only a short period of time has passed since the Horde and Alliance joined forces with the night elves to repel the attack upon Nordrassil. As such, night elves and humans have not found sufficient time to mingle and produce adult offspring. This does not mean that half-night elves do not exist, though they would be far rarer than half-elves. If any exist they would only be young children. They look more like night elves than human. Rare half-elves born of human-night elf unions most often follow a path of druidism and gain their spells from the power of nature. Half-night elves are abl

Half-blood elf is the term used to describe the offspring of humans and blood elves. They do not yet exist. Since blood elves came into existence only a few years ago, they certainly have not had time to mingle with humans and produce adult offspring — without even factoring in blood elf prejudice. This does not mean that it cannot happen, however; it is possible it might happen 20 years in the future. The blood elven half is more dominant, and they have the blood elven racial traits. Like their blood elven parents, half-blood elves are addicted to the use of arcane magic. A half-blood elf must spend one hour each morning in meditation, resisting the distractions of their addiction, or have

Half-human half-ogres are half-ogres with part human descent. Ogres crossed the Dark Portal into Azeroth over 24 years ago, thus, half-human half-ogres may exist. If the rumors of their existence are true, most half-human half-ogres are products of ogre aggressions on human villages. Their primary languages are Common and Low Common. The half-human half-ogre looks more like a human, with rounder ears and pinker skin. Their tusks are also not as predominant, and their eyes are larger. Instead of a mixed blood racial trait, half-human half-ogres possess ogre blood. A half-human half-ogre is considered a human and an ogre, sharing many of the same abilities of both parent races.

:Were you looking for Champions' Hall, the PvP rewards area of Stormwind City, or the Hall of Legends, the PvP rewards area of Orgrimmar, or the Hall of Champions in the Sanctum of Light? The Hall of Champions is a chamber within the Scarlet Halls. It lies beyond the Footman's Armory, and its sole occupant is the Scarlet Crusade's weapons trainer, Armsmaster Harlan. Along the room's walls are memorials of past champions of the Scarlet Crusade. The statues depict the following people: * Arellas Fireleaf * Admiral Barean Westwind * Dorgar Stoenbrow * Fellari Swiftarrow * Ferren Marcus * Harthal Truesight * Holia Sunshield * Invar One-Arm * Orman of Stromgarde * Valea Twinblades * Yana Bloodspe

__NOTOC__ Haldor the Compulsive is a draenei of the Aldor found in the northwest Bank of the Terrace of Light in Shattrath City. He sells specialized flasks only usable in raid zones to players who are exalted with the Cenarion Expedition, the Sha'tar, and the Aldor. The flasks are only purchasable with tokens obtained from creatures in Tempest Keep: The Eye, Serpentshrine Cavern, and the Black Temple.

The Hall of Masks is located inside the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, and is the second area of the dungeon. Named for the giant skull mask statues lining the walls, the room's purpose is unknown, although a trench in the floor littered with bones suggests it had a macabre function during the Atal'ai's height. The Hall of Masks lies past the staircase leading from the Broken Hall, the passages beyond this chamber lead to the Butchery, the Chamber of Blood, and the Den of the Caller. Since the Shattering, the Hall of Masks also has the instance line to the Temple of Atal'Hakkar proper.

The Hall of Bones is located inside the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. It is full of Atal'ai trolls, mummified zombies, and serpents, and is the location of the dungeon's instance portal. The hall is the resting place of several prominent Atal'ai, who have been mummified and buried in sand-filled urns that line the chamber's three levels. The Hall of Bones is accessed via a staircase from the Hall of Ritual, and until the Shattering, led into the instance proper. The instance line can now be found much closer to the surface inside the Hall of Masks.

The Hall of Stasis is a simple hallway that many adventurers have been captured and placed in ice blocks. Horde players will see Alliance mobs and Alliance players will see Horde mobs. The entire zone is frozen, in the most western from entering the subarea a frozen dragon can be found. The area is a testament to those that wish to battle the Blue dragonflight. The frozen dragon might be a statue. In heroic mode only, or can be found here.
Halfdan the Ice-Hearted is the thane of the Winterskorn clan. He seeks "ascension", a ritual which can grant great power to the worthy.

Since marriages between humans and elves are very rare in the annals of history, their half-breeds are rare in the Warcraft universe. Half-races are so rare in the Warcraft universe that Blizzard don't really have any established lore about their potential longevities. Haidene was the first high priestess of the moon. As a child, she heard the voice of Elune.

Half Empty Bottles of Prison Moonshine are found by fishing in the water in front of the entrance to Violet Citadel in Dalaran and the Dalaran fountain. It can also be found in the Slave's Stash in Frostfire Ridge.
Half Full Bottles of Prison Moonshine are found by fishing in the water in front of the entrance to Violet Citadel in Dalaran and the Dalaran fountain.
Hahna Moonscrest is a level 80 tauren druid trainer located in the Sunreaver's Sanctuary in Dalaran.
__NOTOC__ Halana is a night elf hippogryph flight master located in Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands.

Hailwood Marsh is a swamp found in Gilneas, southwest of Gilneas City and very close to the Stagecoach Crash Site and the Blackwald. While Prince Liam's stagecoach tipped on the main road due to an ogre ambush, members of a second coach were not so lucky. Their carriage careened over the edge of a steep hill and into the marsh, where they battled crocolisks to stay alive.
Haiyan the Unstoppable is the leader of the Kargesh clan. He and his clan have gathered at the Mogu'shan Palace, alongside clans Harthak and Gurthan to prove their worth to their king.
Hafuna Landwalker is a tauren vendor located in the Shrine of Two Moons in Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

__NOTOC__ Haephest is a draenei vendor and quest giver located at the Embaari Village in . He owns a blacksmith down in the Arbor Glen where he works with his assistant Vaerdal. He creates some of the finest arms and armor in Shadowmoon, and his wares will fetch a hefty sum in the markets.

The Hall of Chieftains is the center of Thunder Totem in Highmountain, where all the chieftains of each tribe can meet. Entrances and exits consist of three tunnels (Path of Earth, Path of Sky, and Path of Water) and two elevators leading up.

Haephest's Satchel can drop from any mob in for blacksmiths, but most likely to from Karnoth for the quest Shadows Awaken in Teluuna Observatory at Embaari Village. It starts The Strength of Iron, which begins a short chain to unlock The Forge blueprints for the Garrison.

The Hall of Communion is a secret underground chamber accessible by a teleporter from the Makers' Overlook in Sholazar Basin. Long, ornate, and echoingly empty, it is of a different kind of stone than the Overlook, and according to Muradin Bronzebeard, it might be in a different part of the world entirely. The titans built it to watch over the world-soul of Azeroth, and her heartbeat can be heard in the background. At the end of the hall is a room with what look like the large, carved heads of titans gazing out from its walls: the Chamber of Observance. When she attempted to communicate with her Speaker, Magni Bronzebeard, about the impending arrival of Sargeras, Magni came here where he cou
The Haglands is a summit located in Highmountain. It is inhabited by the Crawliac harpies and their Skywhisker kobold allies. Its ruler is the High Crawliac.

Hagatha the Witch is an orc shaman and the main antagonist of the The Witchwood expansion for Hearthstone. She is the one responsible for corrupting the forests around Gilneas, transforming the Blackwald into the Witchwood by awakening and twisting the wood and its inhabitants. She notably serves as the ultimate boss encounter in the Monster Hunt single-player experience. Not much is known about Hagatha's true nature. It's not clear if she is indeed the rumored source of the curse that has befallen the Blackwald, or merely one of its victims. She may have been the survivor of some great battle who dragged herself deep into the forest and fell prey to dark magic, a wicked manifestation of the

The Hall of Strength is an underground area located underneath the western section of the pyramid of Dazar'alor. It contains a few loa altars, and is usually patrolled by Royal Guardians. A passage leads to the outside while another one leads to a locked door that seems to go underneath the Kingsmouth River.

Hall of Fame: Uu'nat, Harbinger of the Void (Horde) is a guild feat of strength achievement that is earned for being one of the few hundred Horde Guilds worldwide for defeating Uu'nat, Harbinger of the Void in the Crucible of Storms on Mythic difficulty.

Hall of Fame: Lady Jaina Proudmoore (Alliance) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Alliance guilds worldwide to defeat Lady Jaina Proudmoore on Mythic difficulty.
Hall of Fame: Queen Azshara (Alliance) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Alliance guilds worldwide to defeat Queen Azshara on Mythic difficulty.

Hall of Fame: N'Zoth the Corruptor (Alliance) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Alliance guilds worldwide to defeat N'Zoth the Corruptor on Mythic difficulty.
Hall of Fame: G'huun (Horde) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Horde guilds worldwide to defeat G'huun on Mythic difficulty.
Hall of Fame: Sire Denathrius (Alliance) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Alliance guilds worldwide to defeat Sire Denathrius on Mythic difficulty.
The Hall of Sorcery is the residence of Margrave Sin'dane. It has three floors, accessible from one another through a Scroll of Teleportation.
Hall of Fame: Sylvanas (Alliance) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Alliance guilds worldwide to defeat Sylvanas Windrunner on Mythic difficulty.
Hall of Fame: The Jailer (Horde) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by being among the first one hundred Horde guilds worldwide to defeat The Jailer on Mythic difficulty.

Haephesta is a Lightforged draenei located at the Stormwind Harbor in Stormwind City after completing the objectives of Expeditionary Coordination. She is later found at Wingrest Embassy in the Waking Shores.
Hailstorm Armoredon is an armoredon mount rewarded from Dragonflight Keystone Master: Season One.

The Hall of Records is the central chamber of the Sealed Titan Facility of Tyrhold in Thaldraszus. Players access it during the Renown 24 chapter of the Dragonscale Expedition storyline. Teleporters to the Hall of Aspects and Hall of Samples are present to lead to those chambers as well.

Hall of Fame: Raszageth the Storm-Eater (Alliance) is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by among the first one hundred Alliance guilds worldwide to defeat Raszageth the Storm-Eater on Mythic difficulty.
Halia Cloudfeather is a Highmountain tauren located in various areas of the Dragon Isles.
Hall of Fame: Scalecommander Sarkareth is a guild feat of strength achievement earned by Among the first two hundred guilds worldwide to defeat Scalecommander Sarkareth on Mythic difficulty.
Hakkari Blood Priests are jungle trolls found in Zul'Gurub. They use blood magic.
Hamstring is a level 4 Arms warrior ability that reduces the target's movement speed by 50% for 15 seconds.

A hanbok is a piece of traditional Korean clothing. Within World of Warcraft, there are a few hanbok dresses that can be obtained, and all of them are sold by vendors in Moonglade, and some of them in Stormwind and Dalaran.

Halycon is a giant red and black worg owned by the Bloodaxe Legion. She produces the orcs' attack worgs with her mate Gizrul the Slavener — despite rumors of their origin being of demonic sources and supernatural works. Deep within lower Blackrock Spire she is housed with her brood of pups in Halycon's Nest and is heavily guarded by orcs and worgs alike.

Halpa is a tauren prairie dog vendor located on the High Rise in Thunder Bluff. He is between the bridge to Hunter Rise and Cairne Bloodhoof's building, in a small hut which faces out, away from the rest of the city.

Hammertoe Grez was a dwarf quest giver located in the outermost part of Uldaman. He was seeking magic for golems as well as the origin of dwarves. He made Hammertoe's Digsite and wrote a message on Crumpled Map when he was being taken by the Shadowforge clan. He had been working with Historian Karnik to discover artifacts of Uldaman. Upon his death, Karnik sought Hammertoe's spirit in order to gain information on the Shadowforge dark dwarves. Hammertoe dreamt about finding the Tablet of Will and Advisor Belgrum resolved to continue in the search. Since the Cataclysm, he can no longer be found anywhere, presumably because the Explorers' League have claimed his body from the dig site, or it ma

The Hand of Gul'dan is a massive volcano west of the Black Temple in Shadowmoon Valley. It is named after Gul'dan, the warlock who aided Medivh in opening the Dark Portal. According to the Earthen Ring, this volcano was raised by Gul'dan himself when he severed the connection between the orcish people and the elemental spirits of Draenor through the words of :the Cipher of Damnation, which were used against Cyrukh the Firelord. The volcano now dominates much of the landscape in the valley. The truth is it always existed, and the spell that severed the connection to the elements also turned the volcano fel. A vision of this act is repeatedly depicted at the Altar of Damnation, near the Fel Pi
__NOTOC__ Halu is a draenei hippogryph flight master located at Orebor Harborage in Zangarmarsh.
__NOTOC__ Hamanar is a draenei master jewelcrafting trainer located on the Aldor Rise in Shattrath City. He is in a building in the back to the northwest of the lift.
Hand of the Overseer is the hand of a Murkblood Overseer in the Netherwing Mines in Shadowmoon Valley. Simply read all of the Overseer's gossip text to receive one.

Halls of the Dead is a defense town hall building of the Undead in Warcraft III. As the presence of the Undead in the living world grows stronger, further modifications to the command structure become necessary. Transforming a necropolis into the halls of the dead gives the Scourge power to raise more ancient structures and advance their cruel efficiency. With continued advancement, the halls of the dead may be further upgraded into a Black Citadel.

Tauren revere nature and, when hunting, they treat their prey with respect. A tauren who requires a powerful weapon sometimes embarks on a complex quest to create a Hammer of Life. A Hammer of Life is a weapon that embodies a tauren’s respect for nature. The tauren spends three days in the wild, meditating and communing with her ancestral spirits. At the end of this time, the tauren scouts the area and hunts the first animal she sees. Upon killing her quarry, the tauren brings its carcass back to her tribe. There, the tribe’s shaman assists her in crafting a Hammer of Life. No part of the tauren’s prey goes to waste. The animal’s bones form the hammer’s haft; its organs, stitched into a skin

Halls of Stone is a 5-man wing of Ulduar in the Storm Peaks, and the home of the Tribunal of Ages and the Forge of Wills.. The entrance is located in the southern part of the titan city by going west until you see the gate. It has a lot of lore closely tied to it. This is one of the non-linear instances in Wrath of the Lich King. The scale of the instance is large, with tall halls and rooms, but is still small enough to move about in without a mount. Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard visited Ulduar and reported that the iron dwarves maintain some presence at the Halls of Stone, with one they questioned about the journey of their ancestor, Mina Stormsmith. The nam

Hand of Protection is a paladin spell that protects the target from all physical attacks for 10 seconds, but also prevents from them using physical attacks or abilities for that time. Players may only have one Hand on them per paladin at any time. Hand of Protection also places the 1 minute Forbearance debuff on the target, and cannot be used on targets with Forbearance.
Paladin Hand spells were short-term paladin spells that gave their target a powerful effect before fading shortly after.

The Hand of Vengeance is the group of Forsaken forces that have been sent to Northrend by Sylvanas Windrunner to bring Undercity's vengeance upon the Lich King. Their method is the delivery of the latest strain of their deadly Plague. They have allied with The Taunka and the Warsong Offensive, under the leadership of the Horde Expedition, in order to oppose the Lich King.

The Halls of the Ancestors is a mountain pass between Njorndar Village and the southern area near Jotunheim in Icecrown. The Bone Witch sent an adventurer here to find the slumbering vrykul hero Iskalder in order to use him in her plot against the Lich King.
Hand of Reckoning is a level 9 paladin ability. It is a taunt with a 30-yard range.
Halvdan is the flight master of Dun Niffelem in Storm Peaks. He only becomes available after the quest A Spark of Hope is completed by the player.

Hand of Ravenclaw can be found near Thule Ravenclaw a bit north of the Forsaken Front. There are only two of them now. They used to be located near Decrepit Ferry on Fenris Isle in Silverpine Forest, but with Thule's eviction from the island by the worgen, they are no longer present there.

The Halls of Lightning Teleporter was an iron vrykul NPC that was temporarily used in the Wrath of the Lich King beta when The Storm Peaks was closed off, thus making players unable to enter the normal Halls of Lightning instance. This NPC was removed once The Storm Peaks was available for testing.
Hand of Purity is a talented paladin ability, available at level 60.
Halo is a priest class talent. It is normally only available to Shadow priests, but will also replace Halo while using Shadow Covenant. It is an exclusive choice node with Divine Star.
__NOTOC__ Hanah Southsong is a night elf flight master located at Whisperwind Grove in Felwood.
__NOTOC__ Hammertooth is a riverbeast found swimming in the waters north of Duskfall Island in Talador.
Hand of Light would have been a level 14 Retribution paladin ability.

The Hall of the Guardian is the headquarters of the Tirisgarde organization, serving as the Order Hall for mages. It is located in the upper levels of the Violet Citadel. This hall was the place where the Council of Tirisfal used to meet, but saw little use after the Council was disbanded during Medivh's time as the Guardian of Tirisfal. The only way to teleport to the Hall of the Guardian is to use an incantation allowing to pass through the protective runes.

The Hall of the Lesser Loa is located on the lower level of the Terrace of the Chosen in Zuldazar. It houses the worshippers of various lesser and foreign loa who don't have their own shrines in the city.
Ham is a hobgoblin located in Rustbolt on Mechagon Island. He is also present during Operation: Mechagon.

The Hall of the Mystics is located in the Vault of Lights in Exodar. The local portal to Stormwind City is found here. The shop is run by mages and offers training in the related arts. Wands can also be bought here.

.]] The Halls of Atonement is a cathedral and area located in eastern Revendreth. They were once a pinnacle of redemption for the most prideful of souls. However, due to recent events they've fallen into darkness and succumbed to forbidden magics. The members of the Halls of Atonement perform rituals of inquisition, of absolution, and of Judgment. The Ritual of Absolution, also called the ritual of extraction, requires a venthyr robe, dagger, and tome, and is usually be performed at a reliquary where four souls may be absolved at a time. Halls of Devotion is a dungeon & raid achievement earned by defeating the following bosses in Ny'alotha, the Waking City.
Halls of Origination Transit Device is a teleporting device in the Halls of Origination.

Hallowed Discernment is a conduit for paladins. It drops from the following bosses: *The Lord Chamberlain in the Halls of Atonement *Sire Denathrius in Castle Nathria *The Prototype Pantheon in the Sepulcher of the First Ones *Valinor in Bastion *Mortanis in Maldraxxus *Oranomonos the Everbranching in Ardenweald *Nurgash Muckformed in Revendreth. An ilvl 145 version is also rewarded from Strengthening the Bond (Venthyr).
Hallowed Silverglass is an anima power obtained from anima caches in Torghast, Tower of the Damned.
Hallowed Candle is an anima power obtained from anima caches in Torghast, Tower of the Damned.
Halondrus the Reclaimer is the seventh boss of the Sepulcher of the First Ones. Upon defeat, Halondrus casts a spell called Return which teleports it elsewhere to heal.

The Hall of the Twin Brothers is the middle level of the interior of the Temple of Five Dawns on the Wandering Isle. While the chamber existed in the Mists of Pandaria version of the Wandering Isle, it was made its own subzone as part of the monks' Class Hall in Legion; in the class hall version, it is accessed by a Teleportation Mandala in the Hall of the Seasons, located to the right as one looks at the statue of Liu Lang and Shen-zin Su. Wise Scholar Lianji can be found here.
The Halls of the Hereafter are the halls past the entrance of Auchenai Crypts. The Auchenai within manipulate the spirits and conduct rituals of dark magic.
Hamma the Butcher is a centaur vendor located in the Field of Ferocity in the Ohn'ahran Plains.

Haomarush was among the leaders of the last remnants of the demon-worshiping orcs, all under the rule of Jubei'Thos and the Blackrock clan. Being one of the lesser Blademasters within the clan, Haomarush was given command over a small contingent of the Blackrock Scouts, which he used to survey the area around the Alterac mountains, where they had constructed a settlement to guard a demon gate. During one of his scouts, however, his troops ran into Arthas, and the dark prince quickly routed and killed them all.

__NOTOC__ Hannah Bladeleaf is an elite rare mob night elf found in the Barrens. Hannah Bladeleaf is one of 4 Alliance Outrunners who are scouting the Barrens. The others are Aean Swiftriver, Marcus Bel, and Thora Feathermoon. The mounted outrunners ride a patrol from Bael Modan in the south to the Lushwater Oasis in the north. The outrunners are elite fighters around level 25 and will fight together. Unless you are prepared or are high-level, Horde characters should keep their distance.
Harbinger Boots are leather boots that give bonuses to strength, stamina, and spirit. Drops off of trash mobs in Scarlet Monastery.
Harb Foulmountain is a rare tauren found patrolling across three small plateaus in the northern part of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. He was on a 5-8 hour respawn timer.
Harbinger Ennarth is a draenei tactician located inside the Champions' Hall in Stormwind City. He offers no quests or services.

Harbinger Skyriss is one of the qiraji entities that the naaru kept locked up within the Arcatraz. He is a servant of the Old Gods and seeks to usher in his masters' vision of conquering all of the worlds in the universe. His plans were surprisingly rewarded when he was picked up by the naaru. He must have corrupted Warden Mellichar into releasing all the prisoners in the Arcatraz. Skyriss uses the same model as The Prophet Skeram, and appears as the 4th and final mob of a multi wave encounter in the Arcatraz wing of Tempest Keep. The encounter is begun by engaging Warden Mellichar. The warden will in turn open the four orbs along the walls of the room, and finally wake up Skyriss. There are
Hands of Power are a pair of quality Cloth Gloves that improve Intellect, Stamina and Haste.
__NOTOC__ Harbinger Saronen is a draenei quest giver located at the Altar of Sha'tar in Shadowmoon Valley. Occasionally, he walks to Anchorite Ceyla.
__NOTOC__ The Harbinger Haronem is a draenei quest giver located on the Terrace of Light of Shattrath City. He is the leader of a group of dedicated marksman regiment.
Hannah is a human child found in Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains where she lives with Alma Jainrose.
Handler Marnlek is a jungle troll flight master located at Sen'jin Village in Durotar.
Hans Crump was a Forsaken Battle for Gilneas battlemaster located in the Undercity during the Call to Arms: Battle for Gilneas.

A harbor, also known as a pier, anchorage, dock, wharf, marina, port or quay, is a place on the seashore for docking boats used in transport of goods and people. Harbors in World of Warcraft are often used to transport players from one continent to another.

__NOTOC__ Handler Tessina is a night elf quest giver in the Tower of Estulan who has Alliance players rallying natural night elf allies like wisps, hippogryphs, and treants towards Feathermoon Stronghold.
__NOTOC__ Harbinger Aph'lass is a n'raqi that resides inside the Stonetalon Peak in Stonetalon Mountains.

Harbingers of Destruction are black dragons seen flying around Wyrmrest Temple in the Dragon Soul and the Hour of Twilight battling the forces of the Wyrmrest Accord. They cannot be attacked, and will never attack players.
